review: 1:2 עֶבֶד הַשָּׂטָן הָרָשָׁע — 'slave of the wicked devil'; the Arabic إبليس has no Hebrew equivalent, so שָׂטָן stands in.

3:4 נַפְשִׁי נוֹתֵן שְׁאֵלוֹת — the Arabic جَمَعَ the two ideas in one construct, 'the Redeemer of the soul, the giver of wishes'; Hebrew splits them across 3:3–3:4 with נַפְשִׁי carried over from the construct.
4:1 לוּ אֲכַלֶּה כָּל־יָמַי — לוּ + imperfect for the wish of لَيْتَنِي; the more common idiom מִי יִתֵּן was rejected as too long for the line.
4:2 עֶבֶד לַפּוֹדֶה נֶאֱמָן — 'a servant to the faithful Redeemer'; ל rather than the construct because the Arabic has an adjective, not a second noun.
